newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money rate rises on stronger demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money rate rises on stronger demand.

text.p: Croatian call money rose a percentage point to 8.0 percent on Monday amid a general shortage of funds after a long weekend.
"We are unable to match the demand for kuna and are at the moment (0900 GMT), 20 million kuna ($3.1 million) short," said a dealer who put fresh trade at a substantial 80.9 million.
Call money deals accounted for most of it.
Ten- to 60-day rates ranged from 8.5 percent to 18 percent.

Interbank demand rose after wage payments before last Friday's bank holiday and festive spending. Banks' balances spiralled down to just 345 million kuna on Saturday, down 138 million kuna from Thursday.
Demand was also strained by exchange operations, partly accounted for by the fortnightly reserve payment due later on Monday.
Banks had some 256.3 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, a sharp rise from Thursday's 16 million, a central bank official said.

The weekend overnight trade totalled 60.8 million kuna sought by 12 banks to cover their shortfalls. Banks lent each other directly some 12.2 million kuna. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb newsroom 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.413 Croatian Kuna)
